prompt: A grocery chain opened five stores in a new state. Traffic is on plan, but the average basket is 30% smaller than in its home state. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: The new stores are likely drawing less traffic than planned.
Rival grocers are probably drawing shoppers away from the new stores.
options.feedback: Traffic is on plan, so shoppers are coming. The gap is what they buy.

options.text: Shoppers are probably visiting less often than in the home state.
options.feedback: Traffic is on plan; the gap is basket size, not visits.

options.text: Shoppers likely use the new stores for top-up trips instead of a weekly shop.
options.feedback: Right. Similar traffic with 30% smaller baskets suggests a different shopping mission. I'd compare basket contents and visit frequency with home-state stores.

explanation: The data shows traffic on plan but baskets 30% smaller than at home. Likely cause: shoppers use the new stores for top-up trips. To test it, compare basket contents and visit frequency with home-state stores. If baskets hold the same items in smaller amounts, look at prices instead.
